label: alg:confinement-sdp
title: Confinement SDP and canonical $T_w$
html:
Algorithm (Confinement SDP — canonical T_w). Solve the LP/SDP that selects the canonical Hecke element T_w realising confinement (or gluon attachment, electron attachment, molecular bonding — the universal ILP of Algorithm \mathtt{def:universal-ilp-algorithm}).

Input

  • Current state x \in H_n(q) (Hecke normal form — Step 2).
  • Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) computed once via Step 6.
  • Markov-trace vector t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i).
  • Target net constraint n_{\mathrm{target}} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}.

Output

  • Primal: optimal x^* \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{\mathrm{cols}(G)}.
  • Dual: shadow prices y_0^* (net constraint) and y^*_i \geq 0 (Frobenius positivity).
  • Active set: \{i : y^*_i > 0\} — the "receptive sub-braids".
  • primal_obj, dual_obj, duality_gap = |primal_obj − dual_obj|.

Algorithm

1. Build LP:
   minimize   Σ_i t_i x_i
   subject to net(x) = n_target,
              G x ≥ 0,
              x ≥ 0.
2. Solve via Clarabel (default) or a sibling SDP backend.
3. Recover dual variables y_0*, y*.
4. Emit the LP-dual witness.

Correctness conditions

prop:operator-selection-lp specifies the LP and proves the canonical T_w is its primal optimum. Strong duality gives primal_obj = dual_obj (modulo solver tolerance); the active dual variables identify the binding-energy shadow prices that feed Step 9b.

Complexity

Polynomial in \dim H_n(q). Clarabel solves the proton-scale LP in milliseconds.

Python API entry point

Canonical compute is the script computations/confinement-operator-selection.py, which solves the LP with primal + dual emission and writes confinement-operator-selection.witness.json. The reusable solver helpers are exposed as pyhecke.lp_dual_solver.solve_operator_selection_lp(t, G, n_target) (in tools/pyhecke/python/pyhecke/lp_dual_solver.py).

Witness contract

Canonical witness: confinement-operator-selection.witness.json. Must emit all of y0_star, y_star, active_set, primal_obj, dual_obj, duality_gap — enforced in CI by lp_dual_witness_validator.py.

Notes

The active dual variables y^*_i > 0 name the "most receptive sub-braids" — they are the structural identifiers of the saturated Wedderburn blocks. Solving only the primal loses this information; the dual emission is required.
